title: Field and density changes are recorded only after they save
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on the Work Orders build under test with Work Orders view permission; the Board View and Tech View display options are on.
  2. The current location has at least 3 lead technicians shown as groups/columns (a technician is eligible when they are Clockable, Active, and their role is not Office or Time Clock User).
  3. On the Work Orders QA build with Google Analytics enabled for the org and a way to observe the events fired (browser devtools Network tab, or engineering/dev support).
  4. Ensure the location has eligible lead technicians and work orders so the displays and fields can be exercised.
  5. Analytics observation available; ability to force a save to fail.
custom_steps:
1. Change a field selection and let it save; confirm one field-change event per changed field.
  2. Change density and let it save; confirm one density-change event.
  3. Cancel a change and force a save to fail; confirm no successful-change events are sent.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • A field-change event is recorded only after a field-selection save succeeds.
  • A density-change event is recorded only after a density save succeeds.
  • Cancelled or failed saves do not produce successful-change events.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043 (Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options). Story reference: SV-10593 — Google Analytics for display and field usage. Spec: Confluence page 845185030 “Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options”, PRD v33 (2026-09-28), requirement(s) S12-R3, S12-R8, S12-R9 (read 30 Sep 2026). Review decisions/answers: Confluence page 853901313 where cited. Source-verified on 30 September 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S12-R3: “Measure field-selection changes after successful saves.”
  • S12-R8: “Measure density changes after successful saves.”
  • S12-R9: “Do not count canceled or failed saves as successful preference changes.”
